central_question: Which External Income sectors can clear the hard wall with royalty/lease/participation/enterprise mechanisms that produce incremental reserved public cash?
hard_wall: External income is not automatically public revenue.

lane_discipline.main: External Income evidence → reserved cash → Replacement Stack
lane_discipline.hyp134: AI abundance → evidence first, modeling later — cannot rescue today’s stack by assumption
lane_discipline.anti_rescue: HYP-134 cannot become the convenient answer whenever current revenue math fails

count_rule: COUNTABLE NOW requires evidence-backed incremental reserved cash. Already-spent dedications and GDP/spend scale are not countable.

mechanisms.name: Natural-gas severance (existing)
mechanisms.reservable_reason: Mostly highway/special dedication; GR slice already in current spend — raiding breaks existing obligations
mechanisms.pathway: None without new incremental yield above current dedications
mechanisms.next_evidence: None for countable replacement — do not double-count
sources: DFA/BLR severance binds prior Use-Depletion slice

mechanisms.name: Lithium/brine severance (Act 1012 / SB568 framework)
mechanisms.rate_note: Salt-water severance rate amended (e.g. $2.45 / 1,000 barrels for brine used as lithium/bromine source raw material) — collections distribution heavily earmarked (County Aid / GR mix); not a free Tax Retirement Fund stream as written
mechanisms.reservable_reason: Statutory distribution earmarks + production not demonstrated as incremental reserved replacement cash; temporary exemptions / incentives may suppress near-term yield
mechanisms.pathway: Requires (a) demonstrated production cash-flow, (b) redesign toward permanent public share / Prosperity Fund feeder without raiding county road dedications, (c) principal-protection if Fund-bound
mechanisms.next_evidence: AOGC/DFA production + collections series after lithium units operate; public-share redesign memo

mechanisms.name: Public equity / generation-storage participation
mechanisms.reservable_reason: Only free cash after debt/O&M/reserves with PUBLIC_RISK_AT_RISK — none demonstrated
mechanisms.pathway: Public or cooperative equity stake → audited distributable cash → reserved Tax Retirement / Prosperity Fund feeder
mechanisms.next_evidence: Candidate project list with ownership %, cash-flow model, legal authority

mechanisms.name: Discriminatory energy export tax / interstate surcharge
mechanisms.pathway: None — redirect to in-state value-chain / ownership capture

mechanisms.name: Cooperative / community food-hub ownership returns
mechanisms.scale_envelope_note: Ag/forestry/fishing GDP ~$2.86B is scale context — not processing margins or public cash
mechanisms.reservable_reason: Only if public/community capital produces audited free cash reserved by covenant — none bound
mechanisms.pathway: Outside food demand → Arkansas processing ownership → local margin → public/community distributions → reserved feeder
mechanisms.next_evidence: NASS cash receipts vs in-state processing margins; hub ownership case studies; AEDC participation redesign pilots
sources: AEDC 2023 GDP report; External Income sector ledger EI-FOOD-AG-PROCESSING

mechanisms.name: Public/mixed facility leases for processing hubs
mechanisms.reservable_reason: Lease net after O&M/debt only; no facility survey bound
mechanisms.pathway: Build/lease food-hub capacity → net lease cash → reserved fund
mechanisms.next_evidence: Facility inventory + net cash survey for cold storage / processing sites
sources: Prior Enterprise ledger — airports/water pledged patterns warn against raid

mechanisms.name: Discriminatory food-export tax
mechanisms.pathway: None — raise EICR via processing/brand ownership before goods leave

mechanisms.name: Existing 2% tourism tax
mechanisms.reservable_reason: Already spent on tourism marketing — cannot double-count
mechanisms.pathway: Only incremental new visitor/luxury mechanisms with reserved covenants
mechanisms.next_evidence: Incremental visitor mechanism design (not marketing raid)

mechanisms.name: Incremental visitor/luxury reserved surcharge (redesign)
mechanisms.reservable_reason: Could be reserved if newly enacted and covenanted — regressivity and tourism competitiveness gates open
mechanisms.pathway: New incremental stream → Tax Retirement Fund covenant (not existing 2%)
mechanisms.next_evidence: Incidence + competitiveness model; statutory draft with reservation clause

mechanisms.name: Arkansas-owned brand / IP licensing returns
mechanisms.reservable_reason: Only if public capital/IP stake exists with royalty path
mechanisms.pathway: Brand/IP ownership → royalties → university / Prosperity Fund path (links HYP-133 research IP)

mechanisms.name: Manufacturing GDP as public cash
mechanisms.reservable_reason: GDP ≠ Arkansas-owned surplus ≠ reserved public cash
mechanisms.pathway: Supplier/ownership redesign first — then enterprise returns

mechanisms.name: AEDC incentive conversion to equity / return participation
mechanisms.reservable_reason: Only if converted deals produce audited returns reserved for Tax Retirement / Prosperity Fund
mechanisms.pathway: Incentive → equity/return right → reserved public cash
mechanisms.next_evidence: Inventory of AEDC deals with conversion potential; legal authority memo

headline.reading: Hard wall holds. Existing public slices (gas severance, tourism 2%) are real and already spent/dedicated. Lithium statute exists but is not countable replacement cash. Food-hub ownership and energy participation remain the top build paths — still $0 until audited reserved cash appears.

build_next: NASS cash receipts vs in-state processing margins + food-hub ownership case bind
AEDC deal inventory for equity/return conversion legal authority
Energy/generation-storage participation candidate list with cash-flow + PUBLIC_RISK_AT_RISK
Lithium production/collections series + permanent public-share redesign memo (do not raid county road dedications)
Incremental visitor mechanism only if new reserved stream — never existing 2%

replacement_stack_feed.rule: Feed only defensible dollars — none this slice

hyp134_boundary.rule: AI abundance may change long-run economics but does not rescue today’s Replacement Stack by assumption
